newsitem.title: USA: Clarcor sees strong Q4 exceeding year-ago.
newsitem.headline: Clarcor sees strong Q4 exceeding year-ago.

text.p: Clarcor Inc said Monday it expects strong fiscal fourth quarter results that will exceed last year's.

However, its Hastings Filter operation in Yankton, S.D. will not be profitable this year and is expected to have an operating loss of slightly more than $1 million. That expected loss is higher than earlier estimates, it added.

"Although we will incur higher losses at Hastings than originally expected, we remain confident that the fourth quarter will be strong and better than last year," Larry Gloyd, chairman, said in a statement.
Clarcor, which makes and markets mobile and environmental filtration products and consumer products, earned $0.48 a share in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1995.

"Our filtration businesses continue to perform at higher levels than in 1995," Gloyd said. "Indeed, Baldwin's fourth quarter sales now appear likely to exceed the level we had originally budgeted, and we see no fall-off in performance at either Airguard or Clark Filter."
Gloyd said Clarcor's filtration products continue to produce record results, led by Baldwin Filters, the segment's largest business.
In the third quarter ended August 31, Baldwin's operating profit improved by more than 15 percent compared with a year ago, Clarcor said.

Sales at Airguard rose by more than 13 percent in the third quarter, despite the elimination of certain unprofitable lines. "Margins have improved significantly over last year and we expect further improvement in the year ahead," Gloyd said.

In the Hastings operations, Gloyd said it will take the company longer than expected to realize cost savings from the Yankton expansion and to rationalize Hastings' and Baldwin's manufacturing operations.

"Nevertheless, we still see substantial cost reduction opportunities in raw material purchases and improvements in manufacturing productivity at Hastings," Gloyd said. "We are very confident that Hastings will turn profitable early in 1997 and be profitable for the entire year."
In the consumer products segment, J.L. Clark had a 20 percent rise in sales and a 29 percent increase in operating profit in the third quarter.
Earlier, Clarcor reported third quarter earnings of $0.44 a share, up from $0.40 a year ago.
